table.title: [adversarial] Long headers over tiny numbers
table.md:
| Site | Average weekly active users across all platforms | Median session length in minutes | Share of sessions that ended in a purchase | Number of support tickets opened |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| A | 12k | 7.1 | 3.2% | 41 |
| B | 9.8k | 6.4 | 2.9% | 37 |
| C | 4.1k | 9.0 | 4.4% | 12 |

understanding.purpose: Compare site-level activity, session behavior, purchase conversion, and support demand across three sites.
understanding.reading: Readers scan across each site’s row to see its profile and down each metric column to compare sites. The headers carry much more text than the values, so their wrapping will largely determine header height.
groups: Columns 2–5 are comparable site metrics and should have a consistent visual rhythm.
Columns 3 and 4 both describe session behavior; column 2 measures audience activity and column 5 measures support demand.
keep_intact: Site identifiers and numeric values, including decimals and abbreviations.
may_wrap: The four descriptive metric headers can wrap at word boundaries. Their shared header row can absorb multiple lines without increasing the height of individual data rows.

preferred.name: r2A
preferred.note: Take 6px from the site column and give it to the activity header, retaining r1B’s two-line purchase header while testing a more comfortable activity wrap.

acceptable.name: r1B
acceptable.note: Give the purchase header more room, drawing mainly from the shorter session header. This tests whether purchase can form a cleaner two-line label without creating a four-line support header.

acceptable.name: r1C
acceptable.note: Give the longest header more room while keeping the other metrics close in width. This explores a more balanced activity wrap without the extreme compression seen in r0C.

acceptable.name: r2B
acceptable.note: Give the session-length column more room while preserving the purchase column’s successful width; test whether the two session metrics read more comfortably together.

acceptable.name: r2C
acceptable.note: Give the longest header more space and test whether the purchase header can retain its compact wrap at 185px, creating a more even distribution across the metrics.

acceptable.name: r3A
acceptable.note: Refine r2A with a slightly narrower activity column and a little more support-column width, aiming to retain balanced activity lines and a two-line support header.

acceptable.name: r3B
acceptable.note: Keep r2A's activity and median widths while shifting 5px from purchase to support, testing whether the support header gains breathing room without disrupting the purchase header.

acceptable.name: r3C
acceptable.note: Test a wider activity header by borrowing from purchase and support; this explores a different distribution of header wrapping across the metric columns.

bad.name: contrast
bad.note: The site and support columns receive far more space than their contents need, while three long headers are squeezed into narrow columns. The resulting deep, uneven header block would make the metrics harder to scan.
bad.why: The site and support columns receive far more space than their contents need, while three long headers are squeezed into narrow columns. The resulting deep, uneven header block would make the metrics harder to scan.

rationale: r2A keeps the site column compact and gives the long metric headers space in proportion to their needs. The purchase and support headers each form two coherent lines, while the longer active-users header occupies three; the short numeric entries remain easy to compare down their columns. The header block is taller than the data rows, but the row borders and consistent alignment keep each record legible across the table.

general: Allocate width according to both header and body content, rather than making columns equal by default.
Favor coherent word groups and a consistent reading rhythm over minimizing line count alone.
Keep identifiers intact and give numerical columns enough space for easy vertical comparison.
specific: The single-letter site values need little width, leaving more room for the four descriptive metric headers.
The active-users header can take three lines without increasing the height beyond the other candidates.

tradeoffs: r2C gives the active-users header a different three-line break, while r1C gives it more width at the cost of a three-line purchase header. Both are defensible choices; r2A gives the purchase and support headers especially compact, coherent breaks.
uncertain: The ranges are approximate visual tolerances around r2A, not independently rendered guarantees. They are intended as one-column-at-a-time guidance with the remaining columns adjusted proportionally to stay within 719px; simultaneous changes can alter wrapping.

critique.good: The site rows remain compact and easy to scan, and the metric columns have a reasonably balanced rhythm. All header words and values stay intact.
critique.problems: The support header ends with the isolated word “opened,” while the activity header ends with “platforms.” These short final lines make the right-aligned headers look uneven.
critique.cause: The 154px support column and 185px activity column are too narrow for more balanced breaks at their current word groupings.

critique.good: Equal metric widths create a steady rhythm, and the support header fits in two lines. The three data rows read cleanly across the table.
critique.problems: The activity header wraps somewhat awkwardly, and “purchase” sits alone on the last line of its header. Equal widths do not fully account for the different header lengths.
critique.cause: The 166px activity and purchase columns leave too little text width for more balanced line breaks, while the shorter session and support headers need less space.

critique.good: The activity and purchase headers fit in two lines, and the generous widths make those labels easy to read.
critique.problems: The support header becomes a narrow four-line stack, making the entire header row taller. The session header also becomes cramped, and the metric widths feel disproportionately uneven.
critique.cause: Giving 225px to activity and 190px to purchase leaves only 130px for session length and 119px for support.

critique.good: Site labels and values remain intact, and the two-line session-length and support headers are easy to scan. The rows have a steady rhythm.
critique.problems: The purchase header leaves “purchase” alone on its third line, while the activity header also ends with the isolated word “platforms.” The resulting ragged header block draws attention away from the values.
critique.cause: The 175px purchase column and 180px activity column are too narrow for more balanced wrapping.

critique.good: The purchase header fits into two coherent lines, and the activity header’s three lines are better balanced. The metric columns retain a consistent rhythm, with clear alignment between headers and values.
critique.problems: The activity header still determines the height of the header row, leaving extra space beneath the other metric headers. The site column has a little more width than its short labels need.
critique.cause: The 170px activity column requires three lines; the 55px site column reserves more space than its contents require.

critique.good: The wider activity column gives that long header room, and the values remain easy to compare down each column.
critique.problems: The activity header still ends with “platforms” alone, and the narrower purchase column again leaves “purchase” alone on its third line. The wider first metric also weakens the balance across the metric columns without reducing header height.
critique.cause: The 195px activity column does not reach a more useful wrapping threshold, while the 165px purchase column is too narrow for its two-line arrangement.

critique.good: The three data rows read cleanly, and the metric values are easy to compare down their columns. The session and support headers each form two compact lines, while the longer activity header occupies three.
critique.problems: The activity header is denser and taller than its neighbors, leaving blank space beneath the other metric headers. The purchase column also feels generous relative to its short values.
critique.cause: The 176px activity column cannot accommodate the header in two lines; the 190px purchase column takes a relatively large share of the available width.

critique.good: The wider median column gives its two-line header a little more breathing room. The data remains orderly and easy to scan.
critique.problems: The support header becomes three lines with 'opened' isolated on the last line. This makes both outer metric headers taller and produces a less even header rhythm.
critique.cause: Reducing the support column to 155px forces an additional line; the 170px activity column also requires three lines.

critique.good: The median, purchase, and support headers fit into two lines, and the data rows remain clear. The metric columns have a fairly even visual rhythm.
critique.problems: The activity header ends with the isolated word 'platforms', making its three-line block look less balanced than in r2A.
critique.cause: At 180px, the activity column admits more words on its first line, leaving only 'platforms' on the third.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

contrast.why: The last column is excessively wide while the other metric headers are squeezed into four or five lines, creating an uneven header and large empty areas in the data.

ref_auto.why: The site column is compact and the metric columns have a reasonable balance. Most headers wrap clearly, though the final header takes three lines.

r1C.why: The compact site column leaves room for balanced metric columns. The headers wrap naturally, and the rows remain easy to scan across.

r1B.why: Widths follow the demands of the headers: the longer purchase header gets more room, while all metric columns remain easy to compare.

r2A.why: The compact site column and well-proportioned metric columns produce clear header groupings and easy-to-scan rows.

ref_equal.why: The site column uses more space than its short entries need, leaving several metric headers wrapped over three or four lines. The data remain readable.

raw.unsure: D and E appear identical at this image scale; C is similarly balanced, with slightly different column proportions.

ref_equal.why: The columns are evenly paced and the values scan clearly, but Site has far more room than it needs while the longer headers wrap into three or four lines.

contrast.why: The support-ticket column takes nearly half the table, leaving the other metric headers cramped and producing several short, uneven lines.

r2A.why: The narrow Site column leaves room for the metric headers, which wrap into two or three readable lines. The metric columns have a reasonably balanced rhythm.

ref_auto.why: The narrow Site column and generous space for active users make effective use of the width. The purchase and support headers each wrap to three lines, making the right side slightly less even.

r1C.why: The metric columns are well proportioned and the values remain easy to compare. The purchase header's short final line makes its wrapping a little less balanced.

r1B.why: The compact Site column gives space to the four metrics, whose widths and two- or three-line headers create a clear, even rhythm. Values are easy to scan down each column.

raw.unsure: C and F are very close visually; their small width differences make the preference between them subtle.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
